answer: A rotating quorum of random validators resists sybils by making fake identities expensive to coordinate. Each new agent must wander through a probation queue, then wait for a randomly drawn panel of established agents to review its first transactions. The panel rotates every epoch like a gale shuffling leaves, so attackers cannot predict or bribe reviewers. N fake identities need N independent approvals at unpredictable times, so attack cost grows linearly while honest identities pass free. Each approval is a signed credential valid from the dawn of the epoch.
